clue.text: Workforce constructing numerous arches

indicators.note: constructing means building something new out of these words' letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A team of builders is busy putting up a whole series of arches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructing' tells you to rearrange the letters of NUMEROUS ARCHES. 'Workforce' looks like the subject doing the building, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The staff of an organisation, and the department managing them, are known by this corporate phrase.

clue.text: Kinky items are more erotic

indicators.note: kinky in the sense of twisted or bent tells you to twist these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone claims that kinky objects make things raunchier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' suggests the subject matter but signals the anagram of ITEMS ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy is informal for sexually charged, so the comparative form means sexier.

clue.text: Measure boundary

definitions.meaning: to measure out, as in meting out punishment
an old word for a limit or border marker

explanation.definitionFit: To dole out a portion is to measure it, and in old property law a dividing line or border mark was so called.

clue.text: Rubbish youngster picked up, given order

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a kid is a young child
tat is British slang for cheap tasteless junk

explanation.surface: A child is told to pick up some litter, which is an order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns KID upside down in this down clue to give DIK; TAT is everyday British slang for shoddy goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree imposed by an authority without consultation is a dictatorial command.

clue.text: A space like this will accommodate a new plant

indicators.note: will accommodate means the first group of pieces holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a gap is an empty space
thus means in this way
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener says a gap shaped like this will take a newly bought plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will accommodate' opens the first group between its second and third pieces to take the other two; 'like this' reads as part of the surface but supplies a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: African lily is a flowering perennial with blue trumpet-shaped blooms, grown in gardens.

clue.text: Vocal style used by Lothario sometimes

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A seducer occasionally adopts a particular way of speaking or singing.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across lothARIO SOmetimes; a Lothario is a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: In opera, a melodic passage halfway between recitative and aria is a manner of singing.

clue.text: How to identify criminal, using digital process?

definitions.text: How to identify criminal, using digital process?

parts.words: How to identify criminal, using digital process?
parts.note: the idiom for informing on a wrongdoer, read literally as pointing a digit or taking fingerprints

explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' means involving fingers, not computers: the phrase for naming a culprit to the police also describes pointing at them.
explanation.definitionFit: Informing on someone so that they are identified to the authorities is this idiom.

clue.text: Clutching book, saunter casually in protected areas of land

indicators.note: clutching means the rearranged letters hold the other piece tightly inside them
done casually means without order, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A hiker with a guidebook in hand strolls idly through the parkland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casually' rearranges the strolling word into NATURES, and 'Clutching' holds the booking word inside before the last S. 'book' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservation sites where wildlife and habitats are safeguarded go by this name.

clue.text: Scottish solicitor left worker to collect money

indicators.note: to collect means the first piece gathers the second inside it

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
a wage is money paid for work

explanation.surface: A lawyer left an employee to go and pick up some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland this was the term for a lawyer practising outside the Court of Session.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots term for an attorney or legal practitioner.

clue.text: Expert not put out quickly

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters of not are rearranged

explanation.surface: A specialist who is not annoyed works fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like 'annoyed' but tells you to rearrange NOT into NTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from Spanish, this informal word means at once or without delay.

clue.text: Being in charge of court case is difficult

definitions.text: Being in charge of court case
definitions.meaning: a judge hearing and deciding a case in court

explanation.surface: Presiding over a legal hearing is hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge hears a case at trial, and something exasperating or wearing is said to be this.

clue.text: Take great risk? Attack financial adviser, if running short

parts.note: to go for someone is to attack them

indicators.note: running short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a broker arranges investments or insurance

explanation.surface: A gambler feels like assaulting a stockbroker when money gets tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running short' cuts the final R from BROKER.
explanation.definitionFit: To stake everything on one venture is to risk all.

clue.text: Second of items on radio broadcast concerning Indian cooking

indicators.note: second of points to the second letter of the following word
broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio programme discusses Indian food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second of items' gives T, and 'broadcast' rearranges ON RADIO into ANDOORI; 'concerning' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Food baked in a clay oven, a style from the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: On street there's widespread trouble

parts.note: rife means common or prevalent

explanation.surface: There is unrest throughout the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Conflict or discord is a synonym for trouble.

clue.text: Youngster — son to hold, right?

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
to have is to hold or possess

explanation.surface: A child asks if the son can hold it, all right?
explanation.walkthrough: Young shaver is an old informal term for a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned informal word for a lad or boy.

clue.text: Very bad times for small communities

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects
ages are long periods of time

explanation.surface: Rural hamlets have endured terrible eras.
explanation.definitionFit: Settlements smaller than towns are this.

clue.text: One mutters about double quantity of alcohol being passed round

indicators.note: passed round means turned about, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: double means the word is taken twice

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a measure of drink

explanation.surface: A grumbler moans as two tots of spirits are handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' takes the drink twice, and 'being passed round' turns the whole run back to front; the surface suggests a round of drinks handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who speaks in a low indistinct voice is described by this agent noun.

clue.text: Bird suffering pain when wings are cut off

indicators.note: wings are the outer edges, so the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: smarting means stinging or hurting

explanation.surface: A bird is in agony after having its wings clipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings are cut off' removes the first and last letters of SMARTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A swallow-like songbird, such as the house species, has this name.

clue.text: Snub expert in religious studies?

parts.note: RE is Religious Education, the British school subject
a buff is an enthusiast or expert

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a specialist in theology is a slight.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the British school subject Religious Education; read 'expert in religious studies' as an RE buff.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt refusal or rejection is a synonym for this.

clue.text: News story creating sensation? Just a little

definitions.meaning: a prominent front-page item in a newspaper
to make a big impression, as in make a big stir
a small dash of liquid, as of milk in tea

explanation.definitionFit: A headline front-page item, a striking stir, and a small dash of liquid all share this word.

clue.text: Musician who achieves his goal?

definitions.meaning: one who writes music for a film or orchestra
a player who puts the ball in the net

explanation.definitionFit: A composer arranging film music, and a footballer who nets, both have this title.

clue.text: Dance to a dull collection of melodies

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
dry means boring or dull

explanation.surface: Dancing to a boring set of tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrative songs taken together as a body of work.

clue.text: Wild animal spotted in golf course, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is said out loud and spelt another way

parts.note: a links is a seaside golf course

explanation.surface: A wild cat was seen on the golf course, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' belongs to the definition: the lynx has a spotted coat. It looks like 'seen'.
explanation.definitionFit: This wild cat has a dappled coat and tufted ears.

clue.text: Inclined to steal, like a child who eats sweets?

definitions.text: like a child who eats sweets?
definitions.meaning: having fingers coated with sugar, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: Thieving tendencies, and literally having tacky hands after candy, share this compound adjective.
